sections.normalized_html:
The two box plots show the distribution of fuel efficiencies (in miles per gallon) measured for two car models.

What is the positive difference between the ranges of the fuel efficiencies for the two models?

The two box plots show the distribution of fuel efficiencies (in miles per gallon) measured for two car models.

sections.normalized_html:
The range of a data set equals the difference between the maximum and the minimum.

  • For Model [MATH: A,] the maximum is [MATH: 42] and the minimum is [MATH: 22], so the range is [MATH: \text{Range}(A) = 42 - 22 = 20.]

  • For Model [MATH: B], the maximum is [MATH: 38] and the minimum is [MATH: 18], so the range is [MATH: \text{Range}(B) = 38 - 18 = 20.]

Subtracting, we obtain [MATH: \bigl|\text{Range}(A) - \text{Range}(B)\bigr| = |20 - 20| = 0.]

Therefore, the positive difference is [MATH: \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}.]
